Figure1A: One price rule connects penalty and constraint views. The graph redirects observed visitation (gray) toward a budgeted target (teal); edge width encodes visits and crosses mark removed hard edges. Clipped graph prices combine with realized-cost feedback before the actor update. Zero graph-price cap gives exact penalty settings. LP and saturated-clip limits require the assumptions in Section 4; the target flow is not executed.
Figure1B: Graph-derived prices redirect learning while one rule connects penalty and constraint views. Observed flow is gray; the target is teal and is not executed. Hard edges are removed. LP and saturated-clip limits are conditional (Section 4). The strip shades median training-cost excess; V ratios report primary summaries: SafePO’s five-seed task median and Bullet’s ratio of means, with 95% intervals (Appendix).
Figure2: Only budget prices cross from the graph target into the actor. The projection reallocates observed flow subject to discounted balance, soft budgets and hard-edge removal. Its shadow prices are clipped, filtered and combined with feedback on realized episode costs. Standard rollout/GAE and PPO/TRPO are gray. The dashed relation marks the target–execution gap, not an executable plan. Feedback is schematic; SafePO uses Adam. Hard masks are optional and absent from these benchmarks.
Figure3: Solved prices reduce learning-time violation versus Lagrangian baselines across both suites. (a,b) Right favors SafeOT-Dual: task-median V ratios (reversed log axis) and normalized final-return differences, with 95% bootstrap intervals. Circles denote SafePO; diamonds, Bullet. Counts show tasks with lower V. Dashes mean not run in that suite; n/r means not reported. † Final task-mean cost exceeds B on 4/6 TRPO-Lag and 5/6 PPO-Lag tasks. (c) Lines are task medians of seed means; blue/purple bands show task IQR. Budget equals 1; Bullet cost uses symlog. Normalizers, seed coverage and per-task curves are in the appendix.
